answer: One effective defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, stake-backed credential rather than on account count. An agent must lock tokens for a fixed period before its votes or reputation updates carry weight; creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence if they share the same limited stake. If detected cheating triggers slashing, the attacker risks losing capital as well as paying the opportunity cost of locked funds. A cedar-and-mesa review thread can document the rule, but the deterrent comes from making each unit of influence costly to acquire and costly to abuse.
